chunks: From him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Ibn Jabalah, from 'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked him: A man had a female slave who was freed, then she married, and gave birth. Is it permissible for her former master to marry her daughter? He said: No, she is forbidden to him.

key_terms.مَوْلَاهَا: Her master (the one who freed her)

ai.seo_question: Can a man marry the daughter of a female slave he freed and married?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies that the prohibition of marrying a daughter-in-law via marriage to the mother (mahramah bi-al-mahabarah) applies equally to free women and female slaves, establishing the 'illah as the consummated marriage bond rather than lineage. It underscores the Shia juristic principle that emancipation does not sever the marital tie's prohibitive effects, ensuring the daughter remains permanently forbidden to her former master. This ruling is foundational in Usul al-Fiqh for distinguishing between permanent and temporary prohibitions in marriage.
